To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the frequency of MBL producing isolates among E. coli strains of healthy children was 1% in the study area.
the high prevalence of antimicrobial-resistant E. coli strains in children without any history of antibiotic exposure is alarming.
The prevalence of AMR, MDR, and ESBL production in commensal E.coli isolates from the children of Khuzistan and Fars provinces, Iran were 54.9%, 36.2%, and 11.8%, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the emergence of AMR in children, especially the MBL genes that are resistant to the most powerful antibiotics and can cause a serious health problem.
the presence of MDR E. coli strains in the community, which can lead to the emergence of carbapenem-resistant strains and the spread of MBL genes in the environment.
the importance of monitoring AMR and the prevalence of MBL genes among healthy children.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presence of MDR and MBL-producing E. coli isolations among healthy children can be an alarming signal for the occurrence of AMR and the emergence of carbapenem-resistant pathogens in the community.
the presence of MDR and MBL-producing bacteria among the children’s commensal flora can be considered as a warning sign for the community.
the presence of MDR bacteria in the feces of children is an alarming situation, especially in children under 3 years old.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the children are not a reservoir of MBL producers but the children are a good indicator for MBL prevalence in the community.
the prevalence of MBL-producing E. coli strains in the community is a serious problem that needs to be addressed.
the presence of MDR and MBL-producing E. coli isolating in healthy children is a serious concern and should be considered as an indicator for the emergence of AMR in a region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of MDR and MBL producers among commensal E.coli isolates in children is alarming and requires immediate attention.
the use of antibiotics should be limited to the treatment of bacterial infections and the use of antibiotics in animals should be monitored.
the presence of MDR E. coli strains and the ability to conjugate and transfer resistance genes to the other bacteria should be monitored in the community.
